panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: 7-month-old patient in CZS review article with MRI T2 axial showing enlarged lateral ventricles and simplified gyral pattern, both classic CZS neuroimaging manifestations. B: 8-month-old patient in CZS review article with axial T2-weighted MRI showing posterior lateral ventricle dilation/colpocephaly, consistent with ventriculomegaly described as occurring in 94-100% of cases.
panels.attribution_text: Ribeiro et al. Congenital Zika syndrome and neuroimaging findings: what do we know so far?. Radiologia brasileira 2017. doi:10.1590/0100-3984.2017.0098. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 5.
panels.figure_caption: A: A 7-month-old patient. Magnetic resonance imaging, T2, axial section showing diffuse enlargement of the lateral ventricles (asterisks) and simplification of the gyral pattern (arrowheads). B: An 8-month-old patient. Axial T2-weighted MRI slice showing asymmetric dilation of the posterior portions of the lateral ventricles (asterisks), constituting a colpocephaly configuration.
in_text_mentions: Enlargement of the lateral ventricles, as depicted in Figure 5, is common, occurring in 94–100% of cases; in most cases, it is moderate-to-pronounced and symmetric; it is accompanied by septations in 10–29% of cases, and occipital horns are commonly seen, sometimes making it difficult to distinguish periventricular cysts(34-43). It should also be borne in mind that the presence of ventriculomegaly is directly related to a reduction in brain volume and can cause the head circumference to remain normal or even increase(34-40,43).
